```{r}
# Reading Dataset
library(tidyverse)
library(lubridate)

# Dataset 1: cleaned_weather.csv (10-minute data)
data1 = read_csv("cleaned_weather.csv")
data1$time = ymd_hms(data1$date)         # Parse time from 'date' column
data1$T = as.numeric(data1$T)            # Ensure temperature is numeric
data1 = data1 %>% select(time, T) %>% filter(!is.na(time), !is.na(T))

# Dataset 2: Weather_Data_1980_2024(hourly).csv (hourly data)
data2 = read_csv("Weather_Data_1980_2024(hourly).csv")
data2$time = ymd_hms(data2$time)         # Parse time
data2$temp = as.numeric(data2$temperature)
data2 = data2 %>% select(time, temp) %>% filter(!is.na(time), !is.na(temp))
```

```{r}
# Aggregating to daily averages (primary seasonality now comes from annual instead of diurnal pattern)

daily1 = data1 %>%
  mutate(day = floor_date(time, "day")) %>%
  group_by(day) %>%
  summarise(T_avg = mean(T, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

daily2 = data2 %>%
  mutate(day = floor_date(time, "day")) %>%
  group_by(day) %>%
  summarise(T_avg = mean(temp, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

```


```{r}
# Step 3: Plot both on the same scale 

plot(daily1$day, daily1$T_avg, type = "l", col = "blue", xlab = "", ylab = "Temp (°C)",
     main = "cleaned_weather.csv (10-min -> daily avg)")
grid()

plot(daily2$day, daily2$T_avg, type = "l", col = "darkgreen", xlab = "", ylab = "Temp (°C)",
     main = "Weather_Data_1980_2024(hourly).csv (hourly -> daily avg)")
grid()
```

START OF PROJECT (USE DATA2: HOURLY DATA)

```{r}
#libraries needed
library(tidyverse)
library(lubridate)
```

```{r}

#get data
data = read_csv("Weather_Data_1980_2024(hourly).csv")
data$time = ymd_hms(data$time)      
data$temperature = as.numeric(data$temperature)            
data = data %>% select(time, temperature) %>% filter(!is.na(time), !is.na(temperature))


#aggregate daily averages to get rid of diurnal seasonality (now only yearly seasonality)
daily = data %>%
  mutate(
    day = floor_date(time, "day"),
    year = year(day),
    month = month(day),
    day_of_month = day(day)
  ) %>%
  filter(!(month == 2 & day_of_month == 29)) %>%
  group_by(day) %>%
  summarise(T_avg = mean(temperature, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

n = nrow(daily)
start_year = year(min(daily$day))
# Convert day to fractional year (ignoring leap days → all years = 365 days)
frac_year = start_year + 
  (yday(daily$day) - 1) / 365.0   # key: use 365, not 365.25

# Create ts object (frequency = 365 for daily data)
y_daily = ts(daily$T_avg, start = frac_year, frequency = 365)

# 4. Plot (exactly like jj example)
plot.ts(y_daily, main = "Daily Avg Temperature", ylab = "Temp (°C)")
```

```{r}
#ANALYZE SMOOTHING COMPONENT
# Step 1: Extract number of complete years
n_total = length(daily$T_avg)
N_years = n_total %/% 365
n_use = N_years * 365  # Truncate to full years

# Shorten to full years only
T_avg_trimmed = daily$T_avg[1:n_use]

# Step 2: Estimate trend using symmetric moving average
# q = d/2 = 365/2 = 182 → use 365-point centered filter (with weights)
# Following pattern: c(.5, rep(1, 11), .5)/12 → here: c(.5, rep(1, 363), .5)/365

weights = c(0.5, rep(1, 363), 0.5) / 365
hatm = stats::filter(T_avg_trimmed, filter = weights, sides = 2)

# Note: hatm has NA for first & last 182 obs
# Remove incomplete years at both ends when building matrices

# Step 3: Create matrices A (original) and M (trend), one row per year
A = matrix(T_avg_trimmed, ncol = 365, byrow = TRUE)         # N_years x 365
M = matrix(as.vector(hatm), ncol = 365, byrow = TRUE)       # same dimensions

# Step 4: Compute average seasonal factor mu_k for day k
mu = numeric(365)

# For days 1 to 182: exclude year 1 (index 1), use years 2 to N_years
for (k in 1:182) {
  mu[k] = sum(A[2:N_years, k] - M[2:N_years, k]) / (N_years - 1)
}

# For days 183 to 365: exclude last year (year N_years), use years 1 to N_years-1
for (k in 183:365) {
  mu[k] = sum(A[1:(N_years-1), k] - M[1:(N_years-1), k]) / (N_years - 1)
}

# Step 5: Center seasonal component (mean zero)
hats = rep(mu - mean(mu), N_years)  # Repeat over N_years

# Now hats is length N_years*365 — matches T_avg_trimmed

# Plot seasonality?
plot(1:365, mu - mean(mu), type = "l", 
     xlab = "Day of Year", ylab = "Estimated Seasonal Effect (°C)",
     main = "Daily Seasonal Pattern in Temperature")
grid()

#HW 2 QUESTION 6
```
